name: Search and papers through the tools
description: Brings the outside in through Tools (Web Search) and Science. Model Plumbing and Learning are the other parts of World and have their own entries.
advantages: One call brings in sources and papers.
disadvantages: Only the web search and papers are brought in today.

name: Responds through every container
description: Responds to a request through Consciousness, Intelligence and the Body and reaches the outside through World.
advantages: One call answers for the whole; each container can improve without changing the call.
disadvantages: It adds a level between the caller and the Assembler, and Body, Intelligence and Consciousness are specifications that no arm carries out yet.

name: Hand-wired general agent framework
description: A team picks a general agent framework (for example LangChain, LlamaIndex or the OpenAI Agents SDK) and writes its own glue for models, search, memory and tools, with each part chosen by taste and tried together by hand.
advantages: Large community, many ready connectors and full control over how the parts are wired.
disadvantages: Every team repeats the wiring and the choices, defaults are not measured and nobody tests the assembled whole against shared cases.

name: Declared sources and enduring integrations
description: Describes the form of the system: where its data lives and which enduring integrations the AI may use.
advantages: A system adopts the parts it needs and declares the rest.
disadvantages: A specification only: each second-level solution has its own implementations, and this one adds none.

name: One request through the long view, the target, the Mind and the checks
description: Reads the long view, translates the request into a target, runs the Mind, and checks goal completion and response quality.
advantages: Each way of processing information can be measured and replaced on its own.
disadvantages: A specification only: each second-level solution has its own implementations, and this one adds none.

name: Representative, priorities and feedback
description: Represents a person, resolves priorities and learns from feedback.
advantages: Each person's way is learned apart from every other person's.
disadvantages: A specification only: no arm carries any of its solutions out yet.

name: One session, three views
description: Takes the session's events once and gives Structure In View first, then Frontend Interface (the run and that structure as plain data) and Terminal Experience (the structure as lines), and hands the interactive terminal entry through.
advantages: Each surface improves on its own measure without changing the contract; a new surface is one more child.
disadvantages: A level between the caller and the parts; the structure is computed once per call, so a live surface calls it again on each event.

name: Target, goal and quality in order
description: Translates the request into a target, checks the goal, keeps working while it is unmet, and judges the response against the resolved quality profile, and reports every step.
advantages: The flow is real code and reports what has no arm.
disadvantages: Only the evidence check has an arm.

name: Cards drawn by relevance from a store
description: Recalls the cards the context assembler names for a query, then the cards the store finds by its words, and fills the store from a folder's files through the card builder, and, given a working folder, the files of it to show first and the folders to leave out (Folder View).
advantages: One store, one assembler and one builder serve every consumer; each is measured on its own.
disadvantages: Recall is only as good as the cards the store holds and the assembler's ranking.

name: The four parts of the Mind in order
description: Runs Context Intake, the Planner, Delegation and the Response Writer in order, checks the Nervous System and Judgment Calls before a risky piece, and reports every step, including the ones that have no arm yet.
advantages: The flow is real code and reports what has no arm.
disadvantages: Every part but the flow has no arm yet, so no response is written by it.

name: Objectives, memory and guidance for one request
description: Reads the objectives, the memory and the guidance for a request and reports every step.
advantages: One view of the long view.
disadvantages: No part has an arm yet.

name: Tier chooser then vendor
description: Asks the vendor the hub assembled with the model the tier chooser measured best for the tier, a model id used as given, and spends the goal record's model calls.
advantages: A consumer needs no model object of its own; cost and failover are chosen once.
disadvantages: Needs a vendor arm and, for a tier name, the chooser's measurements.

name: OpenAlex keyword search
description: Searches scholarly works in OpenAlex by keyword and looks up a DOI.
advantages: Open, citable scholarly data; no model cost.
disadvantages: A keyword query given a whole sentence finds little.

name: OpenAlex semantic search
description: Matches the question to titles and abstracts by meaning, using OpenAlex's own embeddings.
advantages: Suits full-sentence questions; we embed nothing.
disadvantages: Rate limited to one request a second; no run is recorded yet.

name: OpenAlex keywords, rule rewrite
description: Cuts the question to a short keyword query by rule, then runs the keyword search.
advantages: No model cost.
disadvantages: A fixed rule cannot pick the topic words as well as a model might; no run is recorded yet.

name: OpenAlex keywords, model rewrite
description: Has a cheap model write the keyword query through the model-call seat, then runs the keyword search.
advantages: Picks topic words by meaning.
disadvantages: Costs a model call per question; no run is recorded yet.

name: Semantic and web paper search
description: Finds papers by meaning through OpenAlex and adds a web search for what the index lacks.
advantages: Reaches both the scholarly index and the open web for one question.
disadvantages: Two services to reach, and each adds its own delay and limits.

name: Web research
description: Snippet-first web search over the chosen search backend, plus a focused page fetch, returned as citable observations.
advantages: Cheap search results first and a page read only when needed.
disadvantages: Finds pages, not papers by meaning; weak on research-paper questions.

name: Categories of tools
description: Uses a tool by its category and calls the category's entry point.
advantages: A product wires none.
disadvantages: Web Search is the only category with a selected arm that works without a key.

name: Declared and used
description: Lists each declared integration of the system with ``reachable`` (it names a ``tool`` the AI can call and is not marked ``disabled``) and ``used`` (a recent run record lists it in ``used``), and marks the ones declared but never used so they are reported rather than forgotten.
advantages: Says for each declared integration whether the AI can reach it and whether recent runs used it, and marks the ones that are declared but idle.
disadvantages: Reads only the declaration and run records it is handed; it cannot see an integration the system never declared.

name: Declaration only
description: Lists the declared integrations as the declaration gives them and checks neither reach nor use: a list a registry can print, which cannot say that a declared integration is idle or cut off.
advantages: Needs no run records.
disadvantages: Repeats the declaration, so a cut off or idle integration looks fine: the plain registry list the check has to beat.

name: Folder of queued requests
description: Requests queued as JSON files in one folder, taken oldest first and removed once taken so each is handed over once.
advantages: Needs nothing but a folder; any process can queue a request by writing a file.
disadvantages: One source shape; a chat or a task list is a researched candidate with no arm yet.

name: Declared sources, cards kept and built from files
description: Reads a system's declared data through the Card Store and proposes cards through Cards From Files.
advantages: Defaults to local files at a standard location.
disadvantages: Only the local card store and card builders exist.

name: Scoped record edit
description: A correction that names what it concerns (``about``: a record id; ``field``; ``to``: the new value) becomes one edit to that record, scoped to the person who gave it. Feedback that names no target or no new value is returned unresolved with what is missing, because guessing an edit would change behaviour for someone on a misreading. A turn reported as handled badly (structured signals: unmet goal, error, empty reply, work pushed back to the person, unhappy follow-up) becomes one proposed new case for a dataset of badly handled inputs, for a person to prioritise.
advantages: Produces a reviewable edit to one record that Judgment Calls can decide on and ESOI Application can apply, so the correction is kept and is the person's own.
disadvantages: Needs the feedback to name its target, field and new value; vaguer feedback comes back unresolved until a person or an upstream reader names them.

name: Kept note
description: Keeps the feedback text as a note for the next reply: the common way, which changes the next answer and proposes no edit, so the person gives the correction again once the note is gone.
advantages: Takes any feedback text, however vague.
disadvantages: Proposes no edit, so nothing is kept in a spec or metric and the person gives the correction again: the baseline the edit has to beat.

name: Per-person severity policy
description: Proceeds up to the severity a person set, declines from the severity they set and asks in between, to whom they named, with the timing the severity calls for (a medium risk waits and is batched while safe work continues, a high one blocks).
advantages: Reads each person's own thresholds and decides how to ask as well as whether.
disadvantages: Thresholds come from declarations; learning them from feedback needs Feedback Learning.

name: Ask about every risk
description: Asks, blocking, about any step that carries any risk, whoever the person is.
advantages: Never acts without a person.
disadvantages: Interrupts one person for steps they would have allowed: the fixed rule the per-person policy has to beat.

name: Stated and carried fields
description: Orders the candidates by what the person stated and the fields the data carries: what the person pinned first and deferred last, what their feedback implies, the kind in the order the person gave, a blocked item after the unblocked, the person's own rank (ranked first, unranked after), the earlier deadline, the older ask, the more people waiting and the longer since a nudge. Each place has a reason in words and a weighted milestone.
advantages: No model call, no cost, repeatable, and every place can be explained from a field the person or the data holds.
disadvantages: Reads only the fields it is given and the constraints the person declared; a priority nobody wrote down or implied through feedback is not found, and a kind the person did not list comes after the listed ones.

name: As given
description: Keeps the order the candidates arrive in and reads nothing from them.
advantages: Free and instant.
disadvantages: Puts a year-long goal ahead of a today goal and an idea ahead of an ask whenever the data arrives that way: the bound the field-reading arm has to beat.

name: Declared authority
description: Each representative is what was declared for it, a person's or a character's; one with no declaration gets the least authority over the asker's own data only, and its data scope never reaches past what the asker may open.
advantages: Never lends one representative's authority to another; a character with no person is an identity like any other.
disadvantages: Only what was declared; it does not learn preferences.

name: Every declared source
description: Pulls from each declared source (or the ones named), drops a request with no text, a duplicate and a request from another person, and keeps arrival order.
advantages: Nothing a person asked is lost or taken twice.
disadvantages: It only reads sources Body declared.

name: Consent gate
description: Reads a step by rule, with no model call, and sends one risk signal: high for a step that pays, sends outward, deletes, publishes or uses a credential, medium for a step the rules cannot classify, none for plain reading.
advantages: Free, instant and predictable.
disadvantages: Sees only the words of the plan, so a risk in none of them is invisible, and a new wording needs a new rule.

name: Calendar periods and events
description: Due by calendar period in the schedule's own zone, on the days and at the time of day of its window (once per occasion, within its grace), by a run requested after the last run, or by an event after the last run for a reactive schedule; an unreadable time fails open to due.
advantages: A late run never skips the next morning, an evening run is read in its own zone, a window keeps its wall-clock time across daylight-saving changes and a corrupt stamp never stalls a schedule.
disadvantages: Daily, weekly and monthly periods and one time of day on chosen days; an arbitrary cron expression is not read, and an unreadable window is an error, not a guess.

name: Elapsed hours
description: Due when the cadence's hours have passed since the last run.
advantages: Simple.
disadvantages: One late run puts the next morning inside the window and the schedule quietly skips a day: the bound the calendar arm has to beat.

name: Standing work standard
description: A prompt constant of eight points that every unattended recurring run is given and that whoever writes the standing instructions of such a run reads: count acts not reports, act with what the run has, plan around the people as they are, report a blocker once, treat every run as a trial, leave the next step ordered, scale on few tokens, and sample and schedule review. A consumer imports it through the public api.
advantages: Written once and shared, so no consumer keeps its own copy; it changes what a run does outside itself, not when it starts.
disadvantages: A prompt asks and does not enforce: a run can state the points and still not meet them, which the metric's later stages read from the run's own results.

name: One-call assembly of the whole hub
description: Answers a question from what is remembered and from the web, holds the answer to its sources, acts on a goal only when the risk watch lets the step through, and audits the hub for consumer wording; each part comes from its selected arm.
advantages: An end user calls one function; every default comes from measurement.
disadvantages: It asks for every part it composes, so a part that lacks a key or a program holds the whole until that is set.

name: Audit of vendor wording, staleness and configuration
description: Scans the hub for vendor-name branches and reports how stale its research is and how much of it connects by configuration.
advantages: The same audit runs for every consumer.
disadvantages: It finds the terms it is given and no others.

name: Role as the record states it
description: States a part's purpose, what it is not responsible for and who owns that, word for word from the part's own row, and says so when no record knows the part.
advantages: Free and instant; a part and the Assembler read the same words the owner wrote.
disadvantages: Cannot tell when the words disagree with what the part does: the bound the checking arm has to beat.

name: Role checked against the part's calls
description: States the recorded role and adds the contradictions it has with the part's records and code: an owner that names no solution, a part that names itself as owner, and a call its code makes to a solution it neither uses nor delegates to.
advantages: Shows a part doing another part's work, or an owner nobody can find, before the whole is judged from the user's seat.
disadvantages: Reads the literal solution ids of take calls only: a call whose id is computed is not seen; the role words themselves are not judged.

name: Stale areas and one search
description: Lists the areas whose last research is older than the ninety day bar, and, asked for a review, runs one search through The Science and lists the hits as they came: no protocol, no screening, no counts, no grades, no decisions.
advantages: A plain list that a weekly job can act on; the cheapest review there is.
disadvantages: Its review lacks every part of the standard, so the metric scores it as the bar to beat.

name: Systematic review
description: Does a knowledge search as a small systematic review sized to the decision, searches through Web Search and The Science, and returns the investigation record: protocol, queries with dates, counted screening, graded items, synthesis, decisions, the applied part and a revisit date. Reports what learning is due.
advantages: Reproducible and checkable: every part of the record is a rule; an optional fast tier model drops irrelevant results and writes the synthesis, and its failure changes nothing.
disadvantages: Rules judge relevance by terms and dates, so a result that bears on the question without matching a term is missed unless the model reader is used; pages are opened only at standard and full size.

name: Recorded and reused research
description: Does the systematic review behind a memory in the structure: before searching it finds the earlier investigations linked to the solutions the request serves (and the ones above them), reuses a fresh one with its date and limits cited, or searches only the gap of a stale or smaller one and updates the same investigation in place; after searching it records the investigation through a store the consumer supplies, adds each kept finding as a knowledge item of the solution it informs (once, never over a person's text, held as proposed where the location holds it for a person) and puts one scope-fenced context item per investigation. A question that informs no decision is a quick fact: not looked up, not recorded.
advantages: Research is found again by the specs it bears on, so a second related question costs no search and every investigation sits in the structure as knowledge, not only in a log; a failing store or sink never fails the answer.
disadvantages: One extra fast tier call to judge whether an earlier investigation answers a differently worded question; the judgement is only as good as the earlier investigation's summary, and a consumer must supply the three ports for the memory to live in its own database.

name: Local card store
description: Keeps the hub's cards in SQLite, in memory or in one file; search matches every word of the query as a substring.
advantages: Standard library only, offline and deterministic.
disadvantages: No ranking and no embeddings, and a linear scan, so it is for small stores.

name: Plain JSON picture of the session
description: The contract's own dict forms for each event and control, and one snapshot folded from the events and controls: status, goal, what the work serves, latest of each step, helpers with parent and solution, cost, files changed, messages with taken-up marks, the open question, the outcome. An unknown event type is kept apart and never stops the picture.
advantages: Free and standard library only; built on the contract's to_dict and from_dict, so it cannot drift from the events; a replayed or reconnecting frontend gets the same picture from the same events.
disadvantages: A whole snapshot per call, not a delta, so a long session sends more than it must; a frontend that needs live updates calls it on each event or adds a transport; the shape is not versioned yet.

name: Event deltas for a live stream (not built)
description: Would send each event once as it happens with the change it makes to the picture, so a live page redraws only what changed.
advantages: Small messages on a long session; a live frontend needs no recomputation.
disadvantages: Not built. A frontend that connects late needs a snapshot first, and a missed delta corrupts the picture until the next snapshot.

name: Agents arranged by solution, records read on request
description: Folds the events into agents, places each solution under the solution of its nearest ancestor agent, and for an opened solution reads its fields and connections from the records tables (esoi.read_tree) with the latest recorded result of its authoritative metric.
advantages: Free and pure; the same data serves a terminal and a frontend; records are read only for what is opened; an unknown solution never breaks the view.
disadvantages: The hierarchy is the agents' own, so a solution worked on with no agent is not shown; a record changed during the session shows its latest state, not the state the agent saw; the latest result is the newest recorded row, not a fresh run.

name: Whole delegation tree from the records (not built)
description: Would draw the full hierarchy of the solution being worked on from delegates_to, and mark the solutions an agent is on, so a person sees the part not started yet.
advantages: Shows the whole structure the work could reach, not only the part reached so far.
disadvantages: Not built. Large for a container solution, and it shows structure that the work never touches, so the overview is less focused.

name: Live session (reference terminal)
description: Runs any harness in a thread and draws its events in place on a terminal (plain lines elsewhere): current steps, a sub-agent tree, messages sent and taken up, a risky step waiting for y or n, elapsed time and cost; Escape or Ctrl-C stops and keeps the session, resume continues it, and the closing report lists what changed, what is left and the command that resumes. The structure tree (Tab, arrows) and the authority in force open only on request; the header shows spend and time against the ceilings; the soft limit and the hub's stop decision are one line each; a typed line after a run continues the session and `/harness` switches harness between runs (`WorkTerminal`, `ahohs work`).
advantages: Stdlib only; one driver for the hub loop, a stream session or any Harness; every control is shown as taken or not available; the same events replay to the same screen.
disadvantages: Redraw assumes an ANSI terminal (every row is cut to the terminal's current width and the block to its height, so the erase counts rows right); a line editor is minimal (no history, no multi-line); stopping the hub loop waits for the model call in flight.

name: Line REPL (ahohs chat)
description: Prompts, reads a line, runs it through the front door and draws the interim updates, the answer, the summary of the work and any question as plain text. Commands: /help, /trail, /later, /quit.
advantages: Standard library only and works over any pipe, so a script can drive it.
disadvantages: Each line is its own run because the front door takes no history, and the screen cannot replace a line in place.

name: Textual session (full-screen terminal)
description: The shared session driver drawn as a full-screen Textual application (MIT licence): a header, a scrolling transcript of the run, a live panel with the current steps, helpers and structure, an input line with history and slash-command completion, a question answered by one key, Escape to stop and keep the session, a steer shown as queued then taken up (the transcript keeps what finished, the panel only what is running now), and the final answer rendered as markdown with the rich library. One application stays open across follow-ups and harness switches (`ahohs work`); headless it writes the transcript to the stream it is given.
advantages: Scrollback of the whole run inside the screen, mouse and Page keys, input history, command completion and a rendered answer; the same controls as the reference terminal because the driver is shared; falls back to the standard-library arm where Textual is not installed.
disadvantages: Needs the textual library (extra textual); a full-screen application replaces the terminal's own scrollback until it closes (the transcript is printed again on exit); stopping the hub loop still waits for the model call in flight.

name: Polished session (full-screen terminal with the settled screen rules)
description: The shared session driver drawn on a polished full-screen Textual application, brought down from a consumer's long-polished terminal and driven only by the hub's own contract (session events in, typed controls out): the prompt docked at the bottom, a transcript that follows the newest output until the person scrolls away and selects text by dragging, one activity row with a clock once a wait passes three seconds, a calm per-run work panel (about three rows a run, tighter with more runs) and a run detail with the full history and a follow toggle, a note typed while the AI works shown as the person's own line and counted until taken up (several notes combine into one next message, a stopped run flushes them, a failed run starts no new message, and a note is never sent as the answer to a question not yet read), one closing line from structured fields only with the metric before and after shown once above it, warnings folded to one short line each with the rest in a log file, a key line of whole hints (Esc only while the AI works), a command menu with slash completion, and Ctrl+C that copies, stops, or asks twice to quit. A consumer binds its own commands, header segments, panel rows, metric lines, saving and menu choices through the options of `WorkTerminal` and the arm's constructor.
advantages: The rules a person asked for over many rounds of use are kept in one place and each is tested headless; the transcript keeps what finished and the panel what is happening now; the one clock and one closing shape are the same on every harness; a consumer reuses the screen with bindings instead of rebuilding it.
disadvantages: Needs the textual library (extra textual); not yet selected, because the choice of the arm bare `ahohs` opens is the owner's, decided by a presentation metric; a larger surface (about 2,400 lines) than the thin Textual arm; the clock counts from the start of each run, so a follow-up run starts it again; stopping the hub loop still waits for the model call in flight.

name: ACP client session (an existing agent terminal draws the hub)
description: An installed open-source ACP terminal client, by default Toad, is launched as a separate program on the person's terminal and pointed at `ahohs acp`, which serves the hub's session harness over the Agent Client Protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio): each step is a tool call updated in place by its step id (read, edit and run kinds mapped), each helper a tool call titled with the helper and its solution, the solution, milestone, who the AI acts for, the ceilings and the metric before are the first message and plan, a risky step is a permission request showing its preview (approve or refuse), session/cancel is Stop, session/load is Resume, the hub's `_session/steering` extension is Steer (shown as taken up in a message line), and the closing report with the changed files and the metric after is the last message and the stop reason. The client command is set by the option client or the environment variable AHOHS_ACP_CLIENT; without Toad on the path or the SDK installed the arm is reported unavailable and the best-measured arm stands in, with the reason.
advantages: One mature screen (Toad, by the author of Textual) and its keys, scrolling and rendering instead of ours, which keeps improving without hub work; the same client draws any agent, so a person keeps one terminal for the hub and other agents; the hub's loop, stream and native harnesses all reach it through the one agent module; the protocol is open (agentclientprotocol.com) and the SDK is Apache-2.0.
disadvantages: Toad is AGPL-3.0, so it is only launched as a separate program, never imported, vendored or made a dependency, and the person installs it themselves; the screen is the client's, so the hub cannot change how it looks; the protocol ceiling: the structure tree on request, a live spend-against-ceiling gauge and stopping one helper cannot be shown or sent (a client cancels only the whole turn, and a correction is a message line, not a state on the sent message); needs the optional extra acp and a recent Python for the client; the presentation checks that read the client's own screen (rows, contrast, repaints, hints) need the client in a pseudo-terminal and are marked not run unless it is installed.

name: Adopted session (the interface of an existing terminal agent)
description: The shared session driver drawn on a full-screen interface adopted from an existing open-source terminal agent: the Textual interface of Mistral Vibe at release v2.26.1 (Apache-2.0), vendored and trimmed in `vendored_vibe_ui/` with its licence text and an entry in the NOTICE file, and driven only by the hub's contract through an adapter (session events in, the typed entries that interface already draws, typed controls out). It brings that interface's finish: streamed markdown and reasoning, one tool-call row per step updated in place by its step id, the diff renderer, approval and question screens, the helper list and each helper's transcript, the loading line, the input with history and slash-command completion, and a note typed while the AI works shown once as sent (queued) and then as taken up. The hub adds what the base lacks: who the AI acts for in the header, the structure of the solutions the work serves one key away (Tab), time and spend in the header (a ceiling named once half used), the metric before and after and the command that resumes in the closing, each once. Escape or Ctrl+C stops and keeps the session, resume continues it, y and n answer a question; headless it writes the plain transcript to the stream it is given. The screen libraries load only when the arm runs (extra adopted_ui: textual and pydantic).
advantages: The finish of a screen its upstream polished over many releases (markdown and reasoning streaming, tool rows, diffs, approval and question screens, helper views, input editing) arrives without being written here, and the hub's own events and controls drive it unchanged; the widgets stay as upstream wrote them, with the hub's strings and behaviour in a thin binding layer, so the comparison with the project's own screens is a comparison of finish, not of effort; Apache-2.0 allows the copy with its licence and notice.
disadvantages: A frozen snapshot: upstream later replaced this interface with a Rust one, so there are no fixes to merge and every change is made here; it carries about 10,700 lines of vendored Python in 60 files and a stylesheet of about 1,400 lines (the interface it was cut from is 98 files and about 26,000 lines), beside about 1,100 lines of the hub's own adapter and binding layer, in a folder named vendor that the structure rules treat as third-party code; needs textual and pydantic (extra adopted_ui) and Python 3.12 or later (upstream syntax), so the stand-in falls back without them; upstream draws with the terminal's own palette, whose contrast cannot be known, so the arm sets its own colours; a step carries a label and not its change, so the diff renderer has nothing to draw for a hub step until a harness reports what changed; not selected, because the presentation metric decides which arm bare ahohs opens.

name: opencode client session (the stock opencode terminal draws the hub over its own HTTP API)
description: The stock opencode V2 terminal client (MIT, TypeScript on OpenTUI) is launched as a separate program on the person's terminal and pointed at the hub's own server (`ahohs opencode-server`, the package opencode_server), which speaks the subset of opencode's HTTP API the client needs over the hub's session harness: loopback only, a random port and a per-run password, the event stream as server-sent events with a heartbeat and replay from the last event id, a projection store of messages, the inbox, permissions and child sessions, monotonic ids, and the experimental routes the client requires. Each step is one tool call (a read is named, an edit carries its diff, a command its text), each helper a child session and a task row that names the helper and the solution it serves, a risky step a permission request with its preview, a refused step an error row with the reason, a stop ends open steps as interrupted so the stopped state shows, a notice is a quiet row in the transcript, the person's message keeps the id the client gave it, and the closing is the answer, one outcome line and the resume command in the shared words of present.py. Usage maps to the session's cost and tokens as the hub reports them. A client plugin shipped as a TypeScript source file in the package data (copied into a per-run folder, never an edit to the client) uses the client's own slots for who the work serves, who the AI acts for, spend against ceilings once half used, the metric before and after, a correction shown as sent then taken up, and the structure overview in the session panel on /structure. The arm host_terminal starts the server, launches the installed client with the per-run folder (its plugin, its settings, its own data and state, its update check and model fetch turned off), and cleans up; the option mode chooses the full-screen interface or the inline one (opencode mini, into the terminal's own scrollback). Without the client the arm reports itself unavailable with the install hint and the best-measured arm stands in. The presentation metric runs the real client on a pseudo-terminal through pyte at the metric's sizes.
advantages: The screen, its keys, scrolling, markdown and diff rendering are a maintained product's, improving without hub work; the person's usual agent terminal draws the hub too, with the full-screen and the inline interfaces on offer; a permission prompt, a diff view, sub-agent navigation and a transcript of every step come from the client; the server is standard library only (no extra install); the client is MIT, so it can be named and launched freely, and it is never bundled.
disadvantages: The server API is unversioned and marked experimental, and the client calls experimental routes at every start, so a client release can break the arm without a hub change (the tested client version is named in the availability message and another major version is warned about); the client is a separate 258 MB program the person installs (the npm package carries a compiled binary for each platform); the hub copies about 15 request shapes and 24 event shapes from the client with no contract to check them against; what the client cannot show is the protocol ceiling: the hub's own key hints (it says esc interrupt, not stop), a permission row that names approve and refuse, a spend gauge or the structure tree without the plugin, the sidebar below 121 columns, plugin slots and settings in the inline interface, and stopping one helper (no control names one); the client's own footer shows the session cost at cent precision and its own tokens figure; its look is its own: the goal is drawn behind a left bar and not the hub's prompt glyph, and its spinner and border colours fall below the metric's contrast bounds; the first screen takes a moment while the client starts; not selected, because the presentation metric decides which arm bare ahohs opens.

name: Independent views, adjudicated on disagreement
description: Runs one short structured call per view in parallel, each shown only its slice of evidence, counts the draft and any vote the consumer holds, and reconciles by agreement; a disagreement goes to one call that sees only the disagreeing views and must quote evidence that code finds in them. For a reply, each span a view lists is confirmed by an independent call and only a confirmed span is rewritten or removed.
advantages: A cheap model is reliable on a small slice; agreement costs only the views; a quote that is not in the evidence is never accepted; every decision reports calls, agreement and why.
disadvantages: Costs one call per view; a view can be wrong the same way as the draft, and then they agree.

name: Independent views, decided by majority
description: Runs one short structured call per view in parallel, each pick standing only with a quote code finds in its evidence; the pick more than half of the opinions hold is the decision, and only a tie goes to the adjudication call.
advantages: Several cheap samples of one question decide together, so no single sample decides; no extra call when a majority exists.
disadvantages: Views that share a blind spot can still agree wrongly; costs one call per view.

name: Independent views with known mistakes
description: The agreement check with each view's known-mistake lines in its prompt, most frequent first and within a token cap, and a twin view built on those lines while the call cap allows.
advantages: Brings the mistakes already found into the checks that made them; the twin is an extra independent opinion.
disadvantages: Costs a call more per view that has lines; a line that does not pay must be retired by the metric.

name: One verify call over all the evidence
description: One call is shown all the evidence at once with the draft and decides; a reply loses the spans it lists.
advantages: One call; simple.
disadvantages: The way a single verify step was tried before; one small model reading mixed evidence is the failure the independent views avoid. Kept as the bound.

name: Draft as given
description: The draft stands and no call is made.
advantages: Free; the floor every other arm must beat.
disadvantages: Checks nothing.

name: Record field edit
description: Sets the one field a change names on the one record it names, or adds one record or milestone once (ensure-one), in the table its kind belongs to (problems, ideals, solutions, implementations, metrics, quality profiles), at the records location it is given. It refuses a change whose target, field or kind does not exist, whose value is empty or carries an em dash, and says why; a refused change leaves every record as it was, and a change the location holds for a person's approval is reported as proposed, never as applied.
advantages: Edits exactly the field named, says what it was before and after, and refuses a change that cannot be applied while leaving every record as it was.
disadvantages: Applies one field or one record per change, so a change that spans several records is several changes.

name: Append to description
description: Adds the change as a sentence to the end of the record's description: the longer-prompt way, where each correction makes the text longer and no field is edited.
advantages: Accepts any change, whatever it names.
disadvantages: Appends instead of editing, so each correction makes the description longer and the field it concerns is unchanged: the longer-prompt baseline the edit has to beat.

name: Evidence standard
description: Says a goal is met when the outcome is present, declares no coverage gap, was not refused and holds every requirement of the done-standard, by pure functions over the done-evidence code. On the stop question it is the stop-only-when-met alternative: iterate while the last verdict is not met, whatever the cost.
advantages: Free and structural: a set that was not fully processed is never called done by its prose.
disadvantages: It checks structure and named requirements, not whether prose claims are true. As a stop rule it never stops a plateau, an oscillation or a regress, never asks, and ignores what the person stated, policy and the ceilings.

name: Outcome is not empty
description: Says a goal is met when the outcome is not empty: what a flow with no completion check implies. On the stop question it is the fixed-iteration-cap baseline: two iterations, whatever the evidence says.
advantages: Free and instant.
disadvantages: Calls any text done, including a refusal or a half-processed set; it is the bound the evidence standard has to beat. As a stop rule it stops converging work at the cap and keeps iterating on a plateau up to it, and never asks.

name: Pragmatic stop rule
description: The evidence standard's verdict, and a stop decision by deterministic code: stop when the check says met or the next milestone is reached; obey what the person stated (one pass, keep going until, stop) and the policy and authority that bound the work; ask when only a person can supply what is missing; stop at a ceiling; otherwise continue only while the last iteration closed a worthwhile share of the remaining gap for its share of the remaining budget, and stop on a plateau, an oscillation or a regress.
advantages: Free and instant; every decision carries its reason and the facts it used; a person's stated limit always outranks the default; the cost of the next step is justified by the cheaper evidence of the last one (the cascading-conditional idea).
disadvantages: Trusts the verdict it is handed: a shallow check that says met on an outcome with a declared gap ends the iteration early. The thresholds (a 5 percent share of the gap, five unasked iterations) are fixed by hand and not fitted to real runs.

name: Independent review, then the stop rule
description: A second pass that reads only the last outcome, never the worker's claim nor the verdict it was handed, re-derives whether the goal is met, and then applies the pragmatic stop rule on that reading. It is an arm and not a stage so that the metric can rank it against the rule that trusts the check.
advantages: A worker's claim of success, or a shallow check, cannot end the iteration early; free and instant; same reasons and facts as the rule.
disadvantages: Its second reading shares the code of the evidence standard, so it is independent of the worker and of the verdict, not of the standard: a requirement the standard cannot see is invisible to both. It needs the outcome in the history, and falls back to the verdict when none is given.

name: Fast-tier model judgment of the stop
description: Asks the fast tier, through Model Plumbing, for one of the five decisions on the history, with the rules stated in the prompt, and falls back to the pragmatic rule when the reply is not one of them. Built and marked paid; not measured, because the stop stage has no free way to run a model and a metric run for it is not worth its spend beside two free arms at or near the top.
advantages: Can weigh a history the rule's fields do not capture (the words of what is missing).
disadvantages: Costs a call at each decision, and a model's judgment can drift between calls; not measured, so it cannot be selected.

name: Goal record with default budget
description: Turns a request into a goal record: met when the response addresses the request, within the default budget or what its parent has left.
advantages: Every request gets a target, a done-standard and a budget that cannot exceed its parent.
disadvantages: A rule, not a judgment of the right target for a request.

name: Record fields
description: Decides each metric's state from its record fields by code, reads a stale or unmeasured metric through the reader its source names, and adds one intermediate metric for a milestone whose metric moves only through a person, written through ESOI Application after Decision Check agrees the child tracks the parent's done test.
advantages: States come from fields, never from reading text; the intermediate metric is added once and only with independent agreement, so it cannot quietly game progress.
disadvantages: A source proposal and the intermediate metric each rest on one cheap proposal call, checked by independent views.

name: Links held to their evidence
description: Finds every link in an answer and reports each one the evidence text does not contain.
advantages: Deterministic and free: no model call, no network.
disadvantages: It checks links only, not whether a claim without a link is true.

name: Day counts that match the calendar
description: Checks each 'N days from today' and each 'N days before/after an event (date)' against the dates the text itself states and the turn's own today.
advantages: Deterministic and free: pure date arithmetic, no model call.
disadvantages: Reports only: which number is wrong is unknown, so it has no safe repair. Judges only the explicit forms.

name: No em dash
description: Finds every em dash in a response; its repair rewrites each with the punctuation its place needs (parentheses, colon, 'to', comma).
advantages: Deterministic and free; the repair reads punctuation only, never meaning.
disadvantages: Judges one house rule only, not tone in general.

name: Figures held to their evidence
description: Finds every figure in a response that the evidence text does not hold; its repair takes out the sentence that states one, keeping the rest.
advantages: Deterministic and free: digits only, no meaning read; a reply that would be left empty is kept whole.
disadvantages: Compares whole numbers by their digits, so a figure that is derived (a sum, a rounding) counts as unsupported.

name: Network passes
description: One cheap pass per relevant solution in parallel on its generated prompt, then parent passes one level at a time that stop at the first scope with no effect on its children's combination, and one narrow pass per dependent; a consumer's own pass replaces the model pass for a solution it names.
advantages: Each solution is judged on its own records; many small cheap calls in parallel; nothing is cut silently.
disadvantages: Calls grow with the number of relevant solutions and levels; a cheap model can miss a conflict the prompt holds.

name: No structure
description: Makes no structure move whatever the turn: no block, no offer. The reply is the general answer alone.
advantages: Never adds length or an unwanted offer, and never gets a plain turn wrong.
disadvantages: Gives no grounded clarity: it ignores the problem, the alternatives, the metric and the milestone the system holds, and offers to keep nothing.

name: Structure move
description: Builds the block the move calls for from the records first and the caller's draft for what is missing, and at most one offer that keeps the missing pieces as ensure-one additions; a plain move leaves the reply plain.
advantages: Reuses a held solution, alternative and metric instead of adding a duplicate, shows a metric value only when the records hold it, and never edits a record: a held solution gets no milestone and a declined offer is not made again.
disadvantages: Matches an alternative already held by its name alone, so a differently worded duplicate is still offered; the move itself comes from the caller's classification.

name: Rule gate
description: Holds back when the moment calls for the answer alone (urgent, upset, asked to stop, nothing to do with the objectives, raised lately) and otherwise points at the focused or most related objective with one sentence holding its next target and reading, plus the criteria the objective states.
advantages: No model call, no cost, repeatable; every silence and every nudge can be explained from the request and the objective's own fields.
disadvantages: Phrase lists catch only wording they name, and relatedness is shared words, so a paraphrased urgent matter or a related request with no shared word is missed; a model arm may read tone better.

name: Overlap only
description: Points at the objective that shares the most words with the request and says nothing when it shares none: retrieval of the objective with no rules about when to hold back.
advantages: Free and simple; stays quiet on topics that have nothing to do with the work.
disadvantages: Nudges urgent and upset messages that mention the work, and never nudges a thank you, a goodbye or a what-next.

name: Always nudge
description: Points at the first objective with a next target on every request.
advantages: Free and instant.
disadvantages: Nags on every urgent, upset and unrelated message: the bound the gate has to beat.

name: File recall
description: One JSON file per person, a retention period after which items are dropped, and recall by the share of the request's keywords an item contains, damped by age with the newer ahead on a tie; an item that shares no keyword is not recalled.
advantages: Standard library only, offline, deterministic; an unrelated or content-free request recalls nothing and one person's items never reach another.
disadvantages: Matches words, not meaning: a paraphrase that shares no word is not recalled, and a linear scan per recall suits a person's thousands of items, not millions.

name: Card Store recall
description: Items kept as cards in the Card Store (the person as the tag, the time as the source) and found with the store's own search one keyword at a time, ranked and aged like File recall.
advantages: Memory lives where the system's other context lives, so a better store (embeddings, a server) improves recall with no change here.
disadvantages: Inherits the store's matching: the local store matches substrings, so a short keyword can match inside an unrelated word, and each keyword is one search.

name: Recent window
description: The person's newest retained items whatever the request says, as a chat history window gives.
advantages: Free and instant; a follow-up that shares no word with the last turn still gets it.
disadvantages: Returns the latest items for an unrelated request and misses a relevant old one: the bound the keyword arms have to beat.

name: Rolled-up hierarchy and word placement
description: Reads the recorded objectives as a hierarchy: an objective's progress is the share of its units met, its units being its own criteria and its children (each counting its own progress), so a goal rolls up to its parent; it is met only when every unit is, and one with no criteria and no children is met only when it says so. A request is placed under the live (not met) objective whose title and criteria share the most meaningful words with it, the deeper one on a tie, and the answer carries the path from the top.
advantages: No model call, no cost, repeatable; every state and placement can be explained from the objectives' own fields and words.
disadvantages: Placement is by shared words, so a request that names the work in other words is not placed (a paraphrase or another language), and an objective with many words in its criteria can outscore a more specific one with fewer; it never creates an objective.

name: Flat list
description: Returns the objectives as listed with no roll-up (state and progress from each one's own criteria only) and places a request only under the first top-level objective that shares a word.
advantages: Free and instant.
disadvantages: A goal never rolls up to its parent, a parent with met children stays not started, and a request about a sub-goal is placed on the top: the bound the hierarchy-reading arm has to beat.

name: Merge into one labelled view
description: Merges the cards, picked file pieces and offered items the Subconscious prepared with the answer and sources the World brought into one view, each line naming where it came from.
advantages: Free and exact: every line of the view says its source.
disadvantages: It merges and labels; it does not judge what helps the plan.

name: Route to Tools and Science
description: Hands each piece to the worker its tool names (web search, file reading or editing, connected systems, agent sessions, Science), refusing a category the authority does not allow, a piece past the budget or after a cancel, and handing a stop hook to the worker.
advantages: Authority, budget and cancellation are enforced where the work is handed on.
disadvantages: Dollar limits need a worker that reports its cost.

name: Split and route by cues
description: Splits a request at numbered or bulleted steps and at "then", and routes each piece to a worker category by the words it uses (an edit verb, a literature word, a question or freshness word); on a replan it plans only the pieces that failed.
advantages: Free, instant and readable; each piece carries its sub-goal.
disadvantages: Cues are generic English words; a request phrased without them gets no worker.

name: One piece, no worker
description: The whole request as one piece with no worker.
advantages: Free.
disadvantages: Plans nothing: the bound the router has to beat.

name: Plan by a model
description: Asks one model call, through Model Plumbing, to break the request into pieces and name the worker category of each from a closed list, reading the request, the context view, the target, the guidance and what failed last time; a reply that is not a usable plan raises an error and is never repaired by guessing.
advantages: Reads what the request means rather than which words it uses, so a request phrased without the cue words still gets the right worker.
disadvantages: Costs a model call and some seconds per request, and its plan can only be as good as the model; it has no recorded run on the planner cases yet.

name: Id and exact match
description: Matches by id, by the whole name or an alias, or by every word of the phrase being a whole word of one candidate's name (a caller can ask for the whole name only); two candidates that fit, or none, is an abstain.
advantages: Free, instant and readable; never matches a look-alike or a part of a word; abstains on a name two candidates share.
disadvantages: Misses a paraphrase of a title or a post (it abstains rather than guesses).

name: A model judges sameness
description: One model call is shown the phrase and the candidates and says which is the very same thing, or none; an answer outside the candidates offered raises.
advantages: Reads meaning, so a paraphrase of a title or a post is found.
disadvantages: Costs a call; a wrong same is possible and is the harm to measure; needs a model.

name: Most shared words
description: The candidate sharing the most words with the phrase wins; it abstains only when no word is shared.
advantages: Free and always answers.
disadvantages: Matches look-alikes; the way references were settled before this solution, and the bound.

name: One cheap classifier call
description: One model call through Model Plumbing, at the cheap tier, is asked which of information, act, draft or clarify the request is, reading the request and what the Mind can already see; a reply outside the list raises.
advantages: Reads what the person asks for, not the words they used; one call, whatever the request; independent of how the plan is made.
disadvantages: Costs a call on every request and adds a step before the plan; it can disagree with the plan that follows.

name: Route read off the plan
description: The route is read off the plan the Planner already made: a plan that needs more from the person is clarify, a text deliverable is draft, a plan with a worker that changes something is act, any other plan is information.
advantages: No extra call; the route cannot disagree with the plan.
disadvantages: Only as good as the plan; the hub Planner reports no draft or clarify, so a consumer whose planner does must supply the report.

name: Always information
description: Says information for every request.
advantages: Free and instant.
disadvantages: Routes every request that wants work or text to a plain answer: the bound the others have to beat.

name: Cited results
description: Writes the results in order, one paragraph each, then the sources by title and link, and says plainly when a piece was refused or failed.
advantages: Free; every link is one the results hold; nothing is added that a result did not say.
disadvantages: No rewording for the reader's tone or length.

name: Model synthesis
description: One model call writes the reply from the results under the profile's criteria.
advantages: Can fit tone, length and the reader.
disadvantages: Costs a call, and can add words the results did not say.

name: Findings only
description: Raises the findings the code computed from the records (at most three, most severe first) with no model call.
advantages: Free, instant and predictable.
disadvantages: Cannot say none when a finding is not worth raising, cannot weigh a finding against the planned work and proposes no edit: the baseline the call has to beat.

name: Best tier call
description: One call on the best tier over the code-built digest, none when the digest is unchanged, the run is at its ceiling or the watch is off; a reply that is not the JSON asked for falls back to the code's findings. Items are routed through Judgment Calls.
advantages: Judges the findings against recent and planned work, so it can say none, order them and propose a recorded edit.
disadvantages: Costs up to 3000 tokens in and 500 out per changed digest, and its judgment is only as good as the digest.

name: BM25 over chunk text
description: Okapi BM25 over each chunk's text alone: the plain keyword search every other arm is compared with.
advantages: Free, local, exact names and rare words.
disadvantages: No titles, paths or meaning; one word in a long chunk counts like any other.

name: BM25F over path, title and body
description: BM25 over three fields of each chunk (the file path and a generated descriptor, the chunk's names and docstring, its text) weighted 2, 3 and 1.
advantages: Free; a match in a name or a path counts more; the descriptor carries identifiers, headings, distinguishing words and linked files.
disadvantages: Weights set by reading, not fitted; no meaning match.

name: BM25F over whole files
description: The same fielded index with a whole file as the unit, so a file costs all its tokens.
advantages: Simplest unit; no cutting.
disadvantages: A long file does not fit the budget and drags unrelated text; the ablation of cutting at natural boundaries.

name: Latent semantic index
description: TF-IDF over chunks projected to 128 dimensions by a truncated SVD, cosine in that space.
advantages: Free, no model; joins words that occur together.
disadvantages: Corpus-sized vocabulary; weaker than a trained embedding on short queries.

name: Dense bge-small vectors
description: Cosine over local bge-small vectors of each chunk's first 900 characters, cached on disk by text.
advantages: Finds the topic without the exact word; local, no key.
disadvantages: Needs the model once (about two minutes of embedding per thousand chunks cold); the vectors are larger than the text.

name: BM25F and dense by rank fusion
description: The fielded keyword ranking and the dense ranking fused by reciprocal rank (k = 60).
advantages: Exact names and topics in one list; no score calibration.
disadvantages: Pays for both indexes.

name: Local feature reranker
description: The top 100 of the hybrid plus the neighbours of its best hits, reranked by a fixed linear mix of eleven features (fused rank, BM25, cosine, term cover, name and path matches, import and co-change neighbours, recency, length).
advantages: Reads the import graph and the history; no model; weights written before scoring.
disadvantages: Weights not learned.

name: Feature reranker without priors
description: The same reranker with the link, co-change and recency features off.
advantages: Isolates what non-text priors add.
disadvantages: Throws away structure the corpus has.

name: Learned reranker
description: Logistic regression over the same features, trained on the corpus's own history (past commit subjects as queries, the files they changed as relevant), split in time from the test cases.
advantages: Fits the corpus's own way of asking and of changing together; a consumer trains it on its private labels.
disadvantages: Needs a history; recency is not learned.

name: Hybrid that can say nothing
description: The plain hybrid returning an empty list when its confidence (best cosine and term cover) is under a floor set on validation requests.
advantages: No noise tokens for a request that needs nothing.
disadvantages: A floor can silence a real but oddly worded request.

name: Learned reranker that can say nothing
description: The learned reranker behind the same confidence floor.
advantages: The ranking and the silence together.
disadvantages: As both.

name: Model reranker
description: A model names the needed ones among the top 30 of the learned reranker (path and 240 characters each). Paid: one call per request; recorded and replayed through a cassette, not run in this repository.
advantages: Reads the request and the candidates together.
disadvantages: Costs money and seconds on every request.

name: Hybrid that prefers newer items
description: The abstaining hybrid with a recency factor: an item loses up to a fifth of its score by its age relative to the request (half-life 180 days). Reads the item timestamps and the request time; items without them rank as before.
advantages: Newer facts and messages come first.
disadvantages: Older evidence that is still needed gives way to newer, near matches.

name: Hybrid with soft affinity to the request's focus
description: The abstaining hybrid with soft affinity (hubofhubs.the_intelligence.subconscious.context_retriever.context_cards.affinity_tags): an item at home in the request's focus times 1.3, an item from elsewhere times 0.8, never hidden.
advantages: Prefers the focus yet lets an item from elsewhere answer when it is exactly what the request needs.
disadvantages: Needs the items' home groupings and the request's focus; without them it ranks as before.

name: Hybrid with recency, affinity and supersession
description: Recency and soft affinity together, and of two near-identical items from different times the older one is halved (a fact updated since).
advantages: Uses everything free the metadata offers.
disadvantages: Three small weights written before scoring; a repeated fact that is still needed twice is halved.

name: Hybrid behind a hard focus fence
description: The hard-fence comparison: items outside the request's focus are removed from the candidates, as a scope fence would.
advantages: Nothing from another grouping can appear.
disadvantages: Cannot answer a request whose needed context lives outside its focus.

name: Scan of the live sources
description: The diagnostic bound for source access: no index, every request reads every source and ranks whole files by how often the request's terms occur.
advantages: Always as fresh as the sources; needs no build.
disadvantages: Pays a source call and a record per file on every request: fails the no-full-scan gate by design.

name: Nearest items by wording
description: TF-IDF cosine between the request and every item Internal Context can read; the closest items above a floor, best first, within the limit.
advantages: Free, local, needs no history, nothing to keep between requests.
disadvantages: Surfaces only what shares words with the request; an item that always accompanies a request but shares none of its words never comes to mind.

name: What was taken for similar requests
description: Nearest items by wording, plus the items the Mind took for similar earlier requests, each take fading with a 14-day half-life.
advantages: Free; brings back an item that shares no word with the request but was kept for a similar one; an old take fades instead of crowding out.
disadvantages: Needs a log of takes from the consumer; half-life and weights set by reading, not fitted; a model arm (PAID, not built) that guesses what would help is the untried alternative.

name: Folder view and card builder, called as they are selected
description: Prepares a working folder by calling the selected Folder View for the files to show first and the folders left out, and hands card building to the selected Cards From Files.
advantages: Each part keeps its own arms and metric; the Subconscious asks one solution for a folder.
disadvantages: A level between the caller and the parts; it adds no judgment of its own.

name: Records index
description: The esoi library's classifier over the consumer's specification index (lexical hits plus the records each hit links to), each solution with its chain of parents and its dependents from the records' own edges.
advantages: No model call; the records' own index and edges, so a new record is found the moment it is written.
disadvantages: Misses a request that shares no word with any record; the arm the library selects is the one used.

name: Records index, then a cheap model
description: The library's lexical arm gives three times as many candidate solutions as asked for, and one cheap model call through Model Plumbing picks among them from each candidate's name and purpose; each pick then gets its chain of parents and its dependents.
advantages: Finds a solution a request names in other words, as long as the wider lexical list holds it; one cheap call.
disadvantages: One model call per request; picks fewer solutions, so precision can rise while a solution the model judges unrelated is missed.

name: Registry date scan
description: Reads the last researched date of each area in the registry and reports days since, with a 90 day staleness bar and the stale areas.
advantages: Free, offline and deterministic.
disadvantages: Reads the date someone recorded, not the quality of the research.

name: Tier metric selector
description: Keeps the arms at least as good as the tier's held default on public evaluations (anchored minimums) and picks the cheapest and fastest of them by list price and published speed (public_metric.py); passing work per dollar on shared cases stays available as select and pick over measured arms. Role_tiers.py computes the tier of each call role from the same public rows (the lowest tier unless the next tier up shows a significant gain on the evaluations of the role's kind) and applies the owner's hard constraints after.
advantages: Free, offline and deterministic, with the weights, their reasons, the public numbers and their dates in data files.
disadvantages: Only as good as the public numbers (one aggregator supplies every scored number) and the owner's minimums and weights; a leaderboard revision moves the ranking until the rows are refreshed.

name: Anthropic provider
description: Plans, answers, searches the web and lists models through the Anthropic SDK.
advantages: Native server-side web search tool.
disadvantages: Needs the anthropic extra and a key; not measured in the vendor stage while the account is capped.

name: DeepSeek provider
description: DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible API through the OpenAI adapter, thinking off by default.
advantages: Low price per token.
disadvantages: Thinking off by default trades some quality for speed and tokens.

name: Gemini provider
description: Plans, answers, searches with Google Search grounding, fetches URLs and lists models through the Google SDK.
advantages: Grounded search and URL reading built in.
disadvantages: Needs the gemini extra and a key.

name: Multi-provider router
description: Routes each call to the provider that serves its model, and steps to a fallback model on a quota, billing, timeout or outage error.
advantages: Keeps answering when one vendor fails; no vendor lock in the consumer.
disadvantages: Adds a hop of logic; a misconfigured fallback can hide a real fault.

name: OpenAI provider
description: Plans, answers and lists models over the OpenAI chat API, or any compatible endpoint by base url.
advantages: Works with proxies and self-hosted servers.
disadvantages: Needs the openai extra; no native web search.

name: Claude Code CLI
description: Asks Claude through the claude program on a Claude Code subscription, with no API key.
advantages: No key and no per-call bill beyond the subscription.
disadvantages: Starts a program per call, so it is slower than a direct API call and needs the program installed and logged in.

name: Hub text protocol
description: Reads the hub loop's protocol (RUN, READ, CHECK, search and replace edit blocks) and the function-call markup a model writes when it forgets the protocol, including markup that wraps protocol lines.
advantages: Works with any model that can follow a prompt; several actions in one reply; a fixed small prompt.
disadvantages: Off distribution for a model trained on native tool calls: the prompt must teach it, and a model that drifts into its own markup needs lenient parsing; it does not read tool calls in JSON.

name: Native tool calls
description: Reads tool calls in the shape of Claude Code's tools (Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob) as a JSON list and runs each in the folder, refusing an edit whose old text is not unique and a path outside the folder.
advantages: The format a Claude model is trained on: its tool names and fields need no teaching.
disadvantages: Reads only that shape; a reply in the text protocol gives no action; only the Claude Code names are mapped.

name: Either format
description: Takes native tool calls when the reply is a JSON list of them and the text protocol otherwise, so a harness that drives several model families reads each in the format it emits.
advantages: One reader for every family the hub drives; no format chosen by habit.
disadvantages: Two readers to keep in step with their providers' formats; a reply that is both is read as native.

name: OpenAI apply_patch and shell
description: Reads the tool calls of OpenAI's coding agents: apply_patch (an operation with a V4A diff: create_file, update_file or delete_file; hunks located by their context, exactly and then ignoring white space) and shell (the command as an argument list), as a JSON list of calls, and runs each in the folder.
advantages: The documented format of the other large provider, so an OpenAI model is not taught a private protocol; also the executor of the apply_patch tool of the hub's native tool-calling loop.
disadvantages: Reads only that shape. The page does not say the models were trained on the format; the V4A grammar is only partly specified on the page, so hunks without context are located by their removed lines alone; unmeasured against a live OpenAI model (no key here), only scripted cases.

name: Refusal floor alone
description: Runs the command with bash after a floor that refuses sudo, removing the disk or home folder, git push, shutdown, a download piped into a shell and any path word that leads outside the folder.
advantages: No dependency: runs anywhere; the baseline every other arm must beat.
disadvantages: A scan of words, not a sandbox: a program that opens a path itself (a script, python -c) writes outside the folder untouched.

name: Bubblewrap wrapper
description: Runs the command in a bubblewrap sandbox with the whole disk read-only, the working folder and the session scratch folder (bound at /tmp) writable, after the floor; the sandbox enforces the folder boundary so a program that opens a path itself cannot write outside.
advantages: Real confinement without a container or a service; the scratch folder lasts the session; free and local.
disadvantages: Needs bubblewrap on the machine (without it the command runs with the floor alone); the disk stays readable, so a secret file can still be read; Linux only.

name: Anthropic sandbox runtime (not built)
description: Would run the command under Anthropic's sandbox runtime, which enforces filesystem and network restrictions at the operating system level without a container (bubblewrap on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS) with a proxy that filters network access by domain.
advantages: Network confinement as well as files, and macOS support; the runtime is built for the same agents this hub drives. Not built: the metric has no network case yet.
disadvantages: Not built. Beta research preview; a Node program to install; the case set does not yet measure what it adds over the wrapper.

name: One-call MCP write
description: Picks at most one writable operation of an MCP server and its arguments in one model call and runs it.
advantages: One round trip for a single write.
disadvantages: Writes through operations, not files, so the file-edit cases cannot test it.

name: Claude Code, one shot
description: Runs Claude Code headless with a goal and a turn limit and reports whether the goal was met. Drives Anthropic models only (a Claude subscription login or a key); an arm is this harness with a tier, written subprocess_goal_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: A full coding agent with its own tools.
disadvantages: Slowest and dearest per goal in the recorded runs; cannot be steered while it works.

name: Claude Code, steerable session
description: Holds one live Claude Code session per run so the person can steer it while it works. Drives Anthropic models only.
advantages: Mid-run steering and live progress.
disadvantages: Same cost profile as the one-shot runner.

name: Agent Client Protocol runner
description: Runs each goal as one session against the Claude ACP agent. Drives Anthropic models only.
advantages: Mid-turn steering over a standard protocol.
disadvantages: Needs the ACP agent binary, which is not installed where we measure; not measured.

name: Codex CLI, one shot
description: Runs Codex CLI headless (codex exec --json) once per goal with the prompt on stdin and reads its event stream for the report, tokens and cost. Drives OpenAI models only.
advantages: A full coding agent from another vendor, so a consumer with only an OpenAI key still gets delegated sessions; typed JSON events.
disadvantages: Needs an OpenAI key or login; has no turn limit flag (the wall-clock cap bounds it); not measured where we measure, since no OpenAI credential is configured there.

name: opencode, one shot
description: Runs opencode headless (opencode run --format json) once per goal and reads its event stream for the report, tokens and cost. Drives any provider it holds a key for, so one harness serves Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic or DeepSeek keys.
advantages: Provider-neutral, open source (MIT), a small fixed prompt; reports its own cost per step.
disadvantages: Cannot use a Claude subscription login (an Anthropic arm needs a key); a weak model can stop after one refused tool call.

name: Hub's own tool loop
description: The hub as its own harness: instead of delegating the goal to an external coding agent, it maps the working folder, puts the files that matter in view, and asks a pure text completion for actions (read, search and replace edits, run, check, delegate, report) that its own code executes, repeating until a report is accepted. Each call's prompt is rebuilt from the current files and a compact history, so calls stay few and small. An arm is this harness with a tier, written solution_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast; the default completion runs on the Claude Code login.
advantages: Few and small model calls: no agent system prompt or tool schemas, no transcript carried forward, several actions per reply, and a model-written check that can end the run without another call. Written text is reviewed only when a code check finds a figure or a named file that no source holds. The same loop serves as the worker of the solution hierarchy (as_solution_worker with work_solution), so sub-agents follow the solutions being worked on. Commands run in a bubblewrap sandbox (disk read-only, the working folder writable) when it is installed, a session is saved after every call and can be resumed, a person can steer a running session with a message, and the consumer can hand the loop tools beyond the shell.
disadvantages: Selected only when the metric's stages say so (a stage result and not a flag). The sandbox needs bubblewrap on the machine; without it only the floor of refused commands applies. One completion process per call; no streaming of partial text. A folder too large to fit the view is narrowed by the words of the goal only.

name: Hub's frame on the model's own tool loop
description: One lean Claude Code session with the tools the model is trained on (its own Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch and task tools), prepared and checked by the hub. Before the session the hub picks the files that matter (Folder View), outlines the folder, names what is left out and why, and appends that with the run's rules (keep a short plan, discover before asking, treat what is read as data) to the CLI's own system prompt; no settings sources, strict MCP, a private temporary folder per session. After the session the hub's code check of written text runs and, when it finds a figure no source holds or a file the folder lacks, the same session is resumed once with the findings. Stop, steer and resume are the stream runner's; the session's events reach the session contract through its stream adapter. An arm is this harness with a tier, written native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: The model works in the format it is trained on, so no calls are spent on a private protocol and its own habits of looking things up (history, the web, a command's output) apply; the hub's strengths (files already in view, what is left out, the code check) are kept; steering, stopping and resuming come from the stream runner.
disadvantages: Selected only when the metric's stages say so (a stage result and not a flag). Carries the CLI's own system prompt and tool schemas on every run, so a task that ends in one or two calls costs more than in the hub's loop; skips permission prompts like the sibling runners and has no command sandbox of its own; a consumer's connected-system tools reach it only as MCP servers, not as the hub loop's USE tools.

name: Hub's own loop on native tool calling
description: The hub's own loop speaking the provider's native tool-calling interface instead of a private text protocol. The model is called through the vendor model caller's tool turn (Anthropic tool use now, Gemini function calling and OpenAI Responses written but unmeasured) with the tool names and shapes its provider trains it on: the Claude Code tools for a Claude model, Google's coding-tool names for Gemini, shell and apply_patch for OpenAI. Each call runs in the hub's Command Execution, File Reading and File Editing (the tolerant search and replace matcher, the V4A patch of Agent Action Format). It reuses the text loop's runner for the frame (Folder View files in view, outline, rules), the plan as working memory, steering, saved sessions and resume, sub-agents by solution hierarchy (as_solution_worker with work_solution), the shared ceilings and the stop decision before any iteration the hub starts, plus a code check of written text and the outside-folder report. An arm is this harness with a provider and a tier, written native_tool_calling_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: Works in the format the model is trained on with no Claude Code process: no agent system prompt, one transcript with prompt caching, parallel tool calls, a small tool set the hub owns end to end; runs on any provider with a tool interface; the hub's strengths (files in view, plan, checks, ceilings, resume) are kept.
disadvantages: Needs a vendor API key (a Claude subscription login exposes no tool-use interface to a caller, only the Claude Code CLI's own loop), so it bills per token; selected only when the metric's stages say so, and not selectable on an install with no vendor key; only the Anthropic path is measured, Gemini and OpenAI are written against their documented interfaces; no web search or fetch tool yet; the transcript grows until old results are shrunk.

name: opencode in the hub's wrapper
