description: opencode run headless inside the wrapper every harness can share (framed_headless.HubWrapped): the hub's frame (files in view, folder map, rules) becomes opencode's own project instructions, the shared ceilings read its spend from its event stream while it runs, the code check of written text runs after it and Goal Completion's stop decision is asked before the hub continues its session, what it wrote or ran outside the folder is reported, and its tool calls reach the session contract as events. An arm is this harness with a provider and a tier, written opencode_hub_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: An open-source loop (MIT) that drives any provider, with the hub's preparation and checks added by one shared wrapper, so a second harness takes one small class; the Claude Code arm's strengths without Claude Code.
disadvantages: Needs a provider key (opencode offers no official Claude subscription sign-in); carries opencode's own system prompt and tool schemas; steering and the soft-limit wrap-up cannot reach a running headless process (the hub starts no iteration after the soft limit instead); selected only when the metric's stages say so.

name: Hub's frame on the model's own tool loop, sized to the task
description: The framed arm (one lean Claude Code session with the trained tools) with its preparation sized to the task by counts of the folder and the goal, never by words: the rules are the same bytes in every run with the plan rule added only for a folder of eight files or more or a long goal (and the task tools left out otherwise), the files in view are capped at 12000 characters, a folder with no files gets the rules alone, and the code check resumes the session only for a named file the folder lacks. Two plain rules from the failed hard cases are in the fixed text: a file the goal names without a folder goes in the working folder, and a document that cites sources cites every sentence that states a fact. Stop, steer, resume, ceilings and the outside-folder report are the framed arm's. An arm is this harness with a tier, written adaptive_native_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: Built and unit tested, not measured: the hypotheses are in its row of arm_ideas.csv. Same subscription route as Claude Code; a frame sized to the task.
disadvantages: The sizing thresholds (eight files, 600 characters, 12000 characters) are measured on one case set written by one author; a figure the code check cannot find is no longer resumed, so a wrong computed figure is caught only by the model's own care.

name: Hub's frame on the model's own tool loop, with sub-agents scoped to solutions
description: The framed arm (one lean Claude Code session with the trained tools, its ceilings, stop decision, code check and outside-folder report) with six additions, each behind a constructor argument and each small code with no model call. (1) Sub-agents scoped to solutions and no others: when the folder has twelve files or more or the goal is long (counts, never words) the hub decides before the session which solutions the work may delegate to (a list or callable the consumer gives, else the working folder's own records, else the hub's reading, searching, file-editing and response-quality solutions read from its records) and writes one Claude Code agent per solution with its own solution's frame, a compact report form, tools that fit it and the model of its role's tier, resolved when the run starts; a hook passed with the CLI's settings flag refuses any other agent and any call past a budget (an allowlist that fails closed, proven under the skip-permissions mode), and after the session the transcript is read for calls outside the list and the agents' session events by solution. The size counts files, the characters of the files together (forty thousand or more is large, so a few long records count) and the goal; a folder with records of its own is offered an agent for each solution the goal concerns and for the solutions those delegate to, level by level; smaller work is offered only the hub's review agent. The review is asked for by the hub, after the session reports and its code check has run, from the deliverable itself: when the written prose holds at least three figures that no source file holds and no working shows (worked out, not quoted), or one in a deliverable of four thousand characters or more, the same session is resumed once and told to hand the deliverable to the review agent in the foreground, with the request as the person stated it, the file paths and the rule to check every figure, name, date and claim against a quoted source file and to correct or mark as unverified what has none. A lookup, a quoted summary, a table of checks or a code change is not reviewed and pays for no review. The review agent's own prompt carries the request and no milestone framing. The guard refuses a background agent call and any read of an agent's output file, and the note says to call agents in the foreground and wait. Each run's result carries a report of what was offered, what ran per solution and what was refused, which the depth and hard scorers write into the case's row of the runs log. (2) The consumer's skills as a SKILLS section and an MCP config file passed through with strict MCP on. (3) A KNOWN section: the consumer's recall and the earlier investigations of the solutions in scope. (4) Role tiers inside the run: the agents' models come from the role tier table. (5) A step watch: a command run a third time unchanged, and agent calls past the budget, each steer the session once. (6) A frame ordered for the prompt cache: the same for every goal in the folder first, files in view last. An arm is this harness with a tier, written solution_agents_native_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=balanced.
advantages: Built, unit tested and proven once on a real cheap run (a call to the built-in general-purpose agent refused, a call to a solution agent run, a second call past a budget of one refused); measured on the earlier five depth cases and the hard set before the sizing, review and records changes above (no sub-agent was called in those runs: the hard cases were sized too small to be offered any, and on the depth cases the session did the work itself); real probes after them showed the review agent called once on a verification task and catching every planted error in a draft when asked to review it, at the quality tier's price. One measured case where a review changed an answer (a qualitative run on a corpus of about four million characters and twelve computed questions): the review agent found that a parser had skipped table-row voyages, the session fixed it, and two answers changed to the correct values. Cost, as the CLI reports it, includes the agents' own spend (checked: the reported total equals the sum of the per-model costs, the review agent's model included). Closes the gaps of the selected arm without replacing its session: sub-agents by solution with their own tier, the consumer's skills and known context in the frame, a watch on the steps, a frame the provider's cache can reuse.
disadvantages: On work one session can script it adds cost without changing the result (qualitative run, three arms, all at full marks): on a small read-only check of 65 records the arm cost 0.41 dollars and 151 seconds against 0.01 and 29 seconds for the framed arm, all of it on two reviews; on the corpus task with harder phrasing 1.02 dollars and 956 seconds against 0.37 and 361; on a multi-part build it was offered six solution agents, used none because the files were small (right), and cost the same as the framed arm (0.02). Before the review was asked for by stakes, a review launched in the background cost minutes of waiting and one was lost. Claude Code agents cannot start agents, so a solution with child solutions lists its children in its prompt and the top session calls a child's agent directly: the hierarchy is one level deep, not the tree of the hub's own workers. Each agent call costs a fresh context and an answer the session must check. The frame is longer than the selected arm's, and a folder's own records choose the agents by what the goal concerns, so that set can change from goal to goal and lose cache reuse; the hook and the CLI's agent and settings flags are those of one CLI version, and a version that changes them would need the proof repeated.

name: One-call file edit
description: Lands a bounded file edit in one model call, using the context already gathered.
advantages: Cheapest and fastest of the arms on well-specified edits.
disadvantages: One attempt with no tool loop, so it cannot recover from a wrong first try.

name: Folder reader
description: Lists and reads the text files of one folder, never outside it, skipping what is not text or too large.
advantages: Local, free and safe by construction.
disadvantages: Local files only.

name: Brave Search API
description: Searches the Brave Search API through the generic JSON-API backend; the entry is data.
advantages: Independent index; adding it is one data entry.
disadvantages: Needs a key; no run is recorded yet.

name: Claude Code login search
description: Searches the web through the Claude Code login: one headless claude call allowed only the CLI's own web search tool, which returns titles, links, snippets and dates as JSON.
advantages: Needs no search key, only the login the deployment already holds; the CLI's own search tool, with no search service to sign up for.
disadvantages: One agent process per search, so slower than a search API; the results are the model's transcription of the tool's results, so a link can be mistranscribed; subject to the login's usage limits; declared paid because every call is a model call; named in the settings, never chosen automatically.

name: Gemini grounding
description: Searches through Gemini's Google Search grounding tool and resolves the redirect links to the real pages.
advantages: Needs only a Gemini key; free up to a daily limit of grounded prompts.
disadvantages: Ties the search to one vendor's model and quota.

name: Provider-native search
description: Wraps any model provider object that exposes web_search(query, model, max_results).
advantages: Reuses a provider the consumer already has.
disadvantages: Quality and shape depend on the provider; a link may arrive unresolved.

name: SearXNG metasearch
description: Searches a self-hosted SearXNG instance by base url.
advantages: Open source and self-hosted, no per-query fee.
disadvantages: Needs an instance to run and keep; no run is recorded yet.

name: Serper Google search
description: Searches the Serper API through the generic JSON-API backend; the entry is data.
advantages: One data entry to add.
disadvantages: Needs a key; no run is recorded yet.

name: Tavily search API
description: Searches the Tavily API through the generic JSON-API backend; the entry is data.
advantages: Built for agent use; one data entry to add.
disadvantages: Needs a key; no run is recorded yet.

name: Model-written topic cards
description: Walks the folder, picks representative files per area and asks a model to propose topic cards that name what people ask about, then removes duplicates.
advantages: Cards carry the words a person would search for, which no structure-only tool can know.
disadvantages: Costs model calls on every build, and its grouping depends on the model and the sampled files.

name: One card per file
description: BASELINE for finding a file: one card per source file, described by its docstrings and symbols. A floor to beat on file finding, not a card builder: a card per file is an index of files and is not what a card store keeps.
advantages: Free, deterministic and fast; a file is never hidden behind a group.
disadvantages: As many cards as files (above the cap of the topic-needs metric), and no grouping, so a question about a topic has to hit the right file's own words.

name: Graphify file groups
description: Runs Graphify's code-only extraction, collapses its symbol graph to a graph of files, and makes one card per community of files.
advantages: Free and offline (tree-sitter, no model); groups files by real calls, imports and inheritance.
disadvantages: Groups by structure, not by how people ask; group sizes are uneven, and it adds a pinned third-party dependency.

name: File plus topic cards
description: The one-card-per-file floor plus the persisted topic cards (their ids prefixed ``topic-``): the selector can pick a file's own card or a topic card, whichever ranks higher for the task. No model is called.
advantages: Free; keeps every file reachable through its own card and adds the topic names a model wrote, which a file card lacks.
disadvantages: The topic cards are one recorded build of the pinned corpus, so it runs only on that corpus; a new corpus needs a new paid build of llm_topic_cards first. It keeps a card per file, so its store is above the cap of the topic-needs metric.

name: Topic cards replay
description: The topic cards of one recorded paid build of ``llm_topic_cards``, returned as recorded: a replay, not a new build. It calls no model.
advantages: Free and exact: it reproduces the recorded result of the paid build, so the number can be checked without paying again.
disadvantages: Not a builder for any other corpus: it refuses one, and its cards cover only 102 of the 892 files, so it is a record of what the paid build scored and not a builder to ship.

name: Cochange topic cards
description: Topic cards from co-change: files changed together in at least ``min_support`` commits of a recorded history are one card (at most ``cap`` files, a file in one card); the commit subjects that changed them together are the card's topic words; files with no co-change get folder cards when ``backfill`` is true.
advantages: Free, deterministic and fast; groups files by the work people really did on them together and names each card in the words of the commits that changed them; every card is within a size cap and a file is in one card, so the store stays far under a card per file.
disadvantages: Needs a history of changes to learn from and knows nothing of a file that never changed with another; files with no co-change fall back to folder cards.

name: Import graph topic cards
description: Topic cards from the import graph: files that import each other are one card (at most ``cap`` files, a file in one card), the most connected pairs first; files that import nothing in the corpus get folder cards when ``backfill`` is true.
advantages: Free, deterministic and needs only the source it is handed (no history, no model); groups files that import each other, which is how code is wired into a topic.
disadvantages: Groups by structure and not by how people ask, so a card carries no topic words beyond its files' own; files that import nothing in the corpus fall back to folder cards.

name: Names, whole folder, shared words (the harness as it was)
description: The selection the hub's work harness used before this solution: skip a fixed list of folder names, hidden folders and virtual environments; show the files the goal names, then the whole folder when it fits, then for a small folder a few files sharing words with the goal, and nothing unasked for a corpus of more than 200 files.
advantages: Free; exactly what ran in production, so it is the floor every arm must beat; fast.
disadvantages: Walks into build output, vendored code and credential folders because only three names are skipped; a corpus gets nothing unasked, so a file the goal describes but does not name is missed; reports only what its name list skipped.

name: Folders judged by evidence, files ranked by what the work points at
description: Judges each folder by a table of markers and rules (a project file beside it, a marker inside it, what its files are, the project's own .gitignore) and leaves out dependency, build, cache, generated and risky places with the reason; ranks the rest by rare goal words in the path, headings and opening, the work's own ids and quoted strings, links from a named file, the trail of earlier runs and the newest of a numbered series.
advantages: Free and local; a new ecosystem is one row of the marker table; a risky folder is never read and a file named inside one comes back flagged; works for a corpus of thousands of files.
disadvantages: Its weights are fixed by reading and tuned on invented cases; a goal in words that appear in no file (a synonym) finds nothing; reads the first 2 KB of every kept file; the marker table cannot know a tool it has no row for, though a .gitignore, a cache marker and an environment marker catch most.

name: Evidence candidates, then one cheap model call
description: Takes the evidence arm's wider candidate list (up to 30 files with size and first heading) and asks one fast-tier model call to name the files the work needs; the files the goal names and the flagged ones stay as they were.
advantages: Can bridge a goal and a file that share no word; one call, small prompt.
disadvantages: Paid and slower; the model sees only the candidate list, so it cannot find a file the evidence arm did not rank; not yet measured against the free arm.
